root_cause.text: In the sched/mmcid fork path, sched_mm_cid_fork() registered a new task as an mm_cid user and assigned it a CID before the task was visible in the thread/global task lists, so concurrent mm_cid_fixup_tasks_to_cpus() iteration could miss that task and leave CID accounting inconsistent, causing schedule-in stalls.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states “A newly forked task is accounted as MMCID user before the task is visible,” describes mm_cid_fixup_tasks_to_cpus() failing because “tnew1 is not visible yet,” and the patch fixes this by removing sched_mm_cid_fork(tsk) from copy_mm() and calling it later in sched_post_fork() after task visibility.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused or obsolete `sched_mm_cid_fork()` declaration from the `CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID` interface.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the declaration of the function prototype `void sched_mm_cid_fork(struct task_struct *t);` from the `#ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID` section, while leaving the other `sched_mm_cid_*` declarations unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this change has no direct effect by itself; it stops exposing `sched_mm_cid_fork()` through this header/interface, which likely reflects that the function is no longer used, defined elsewhere differently, or should no longer be called from code including this header.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the unused no-op sched_mm_cid_fork() stub from the disabled-config path to keep the stub API consistent with current scheduler MM CID usage.
intent_record.what: In the #else stub section, the empty static inline function definition for sched_mm_cid_fork(struct task_struct *t) was removed, while the neighboring no-op stubs for sched_mm_cid_before_execve, sched_mm_cid_after_execve, and sched_mm_cid_exit remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: When this #else configuration is active, code can no longer call a local no-op sched_mm_cid_fork() stub from this header, which aligns the available API with code that no longer needs or should expose that fork hook in this configuration; runtime behavior is otherwise unchanged because the removed function had an empty body.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove sched_mm_cid_fork() from copy_mm() so fork-time scheduler mm CID handling is no longer performed in this memory-copy path.
intent_record.what: The call to sched_mm_cid_fork(tsk); was removed from copy_mm() after assigning tsk->mm and tsk->active_mm, leaving the function to return 0 immediately.
intent_record.how: At runtime, fork-time scheduler mm CID initialization or handling for the new task no longer occurs in copy_mm(), preventing that scheduler-specific operation from being executed at this point in process memory setup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove sched_mm_cid_exit() from copy_process() failure cleanup to avoid incorrect mm-cid teardown on the bad fork path.
intent_record.what: The call to sched_mm_cid_exit(p); was removed from the bad_fork_cleanup_mm error-handling block inside copy_process(), while the surrounding mm cleanup calls mm_clear_owner(p->mm, p); and mmput(p->mm); remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when process creation fails and execution reaches bad_fork_cleanup_mm, the kernel no longer invokes sched_mm_cid_exit() for the partially created task before clearing the mm owner and dropping the mm reference. This changes the failure-path cleanup behavior by avoiding that scheduler/mm-cid teardown step in this context.

intent_record.intent_summary: Invoke sched_mm_cid_fork() during sched_post_fork() so new tasks receive the required mm_cid-related post-fork scheduler initialization.
intent_record.what: A forward declaration for static void sched_mm_cid_fork(struct task_struct *t); was added before sched_post_fork(), and sched_post_fork() was modified to call sched_mm_cid_fork(p) at the start of the function before uclamp_post_fork(p) and scx_post_fork(p).
intent_record.how: At runtime, every task reaching sched_post_fork() will now also execute sched_mm_cid_fork() during post-fork scheduler setup, adding previously missing fork-time initialization or handling related to mm_cid for the new task before the existing post-fork hooks run.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix mm_cid task-to-CPU fixup accounting by subtracting only the transferred caller and keeping the incoming active task counted.
intent_record.what: The code changes the initial user count calculation in mm_cid_do_fixup_tasks_to_cpus() from `mm->mm_cid.users - 2` to `mm->mm_cid.users - 1`, removes the immediate `if (!users) return;` early return, and updates the surrounding comment to describe that only the caller is subtracted while the incoming task remains accounted for even though its cid is still UNSET.
intent_record.how: At runtime this changes the accounting baseline so the function no longer excludes both the caller and the incoming task from `mm->mm_cid.users`; instead it excludes only the caller and continues processing even when that leaves zero remaining users. This fixes thread/user accounting during task-to-CPU fixup so the visible incoming task with active mm_cid is still counted correctly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early NULL-mm guard in sched_mm_cid_fork to avoid invalid access while keeping the CID state warning and restricting the helper to file-local scope.
intent_record.what: The function declaration for sched_mm_cid_fork was changed from global to static, and the combined warning check `WARN_ON_ONCE(!mm || t->mm_cid.cid != MM_CID_UNSET);` was split so that the function now returns immediately when `t->mm` is NULL and only warns when `t->mm_cid.cid` is not `MM_CID_UNSET`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now safely exits for tasks without an mm_struct instead of continuing after a warning and dereferencing `mm`, which prevents invalid access while preserving the warning for unexpected non-unset CID state. Making the function static also limits its visibility to the defining translation unit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a no-op sched_mm_cid_fork() stub for non-CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID builds so callers compile cleanly without affecting runtime behavior.
intent_record.what: In the !CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID fallback section, a new empty static inline function definition was added: sched_mm_cid_fork(struct task_struct *t) { }.
intent_record.how: This provides a no-op stub for sched_mm_cid_fork() when CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID is disabled, allowing code that calls this function to compile and link in that configuration without changing runtime behavior.

consistency_review.core_intent: Remove the obsolete sched_mm_cid_fork() API and its invocation so fork-time scheduler MM CID handling is no longer part of the copy_mm/fork path.

Fix mm_cid fork-path handling in the scheduler by moving task initialization to the proper post-fork hook, avoiding incorrect cleanup on failed forks, and providing a non-CONFIG_SCHED_MM_CID stub so the new call site always compiles.

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability is specifically caused by sched_mm_cid_fork() assigning/registering MM CID state too early during fork. This group removes that API and its fork-path invocation, directly eliminating the buggy behavior from copy_mm()/fork and thus addressing the root cause.

The changes directly adjust the mm_cid fork-path initialization by moving sched_mm_cid_fork() to the post-fork stage, which matches the root cause of assigning/registering mm_cid too early before task visibility. The cleanup and stub changes support that fix and correct related fork-path behavior.

This change directly targets mm_cid fixup task-to-CPU accounting consistency, which is part of the same failure mode as the root cause. Adjusting the fixup accounting to avoid dropping the incoming active task addresses the inconsistent CID/task accounting that could result from the fork/fixup race.

The root cause is incorrect fork-time CID registration ordering relative to task list visibility, causing races with mm_cid_fixup_tasks_to_cpus(). This group only adds a NULL-mm guard and limits helper scope, which addresses invalid access/hardening rather than the registration-order race or CID accounting inconsistency.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct vulnerable action: it performs mm_cid fork registration during copy_mm(), before the new task is visible in task lists, creating the race where concurrent mm_cid_fixup_tasks_to_cpus() iteration can miss the task and corrupt CID accounting.

This declaration represents the obsolete fork-time API whose use enabled the premature mm_cid registration in the fork/mm path. While not the runtime bug itself, it is part of the vulnerable design that allowed the incorrect call site.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs mm_cid fork registration in copy_mm(), assigning/registering the new task as an mm_cid user before the task is visible in the task lists. That ordering creates the race where concurrent mm_cid_fixup_tasks_to_cpus() iteration can miss the task and leave CID accounting inconsistent, leading to schedule-in stalls.
